canonical_name: padasip 1.2.2 -- adaptive filters (LMS, NLMS, RLS, AP, GNGD) and adaptive system identification in Python (Matous Cejnek)
lineage: Widrow & Hoff's LMS (1960; the ADALINE rule) and its descendants -- normalised LMS, recursive least squares, affine projection -- as a small library for adaptive filtering, prediction and system identification. Genuinely ADAPTIVE: weights change online in response to error. Recorded honestly as an adaptive FILTER/identifier, not a closed-loop controller (the charter's 'genuinely adaptive controller' with pinned provenance was not found this batch; see the report).

example.command: python harness: identify an unknown 4-tap FIR plant from input/output pairs with NLMS and RLS
example.input: a known plant driven by noise
example.output: recovered taps within tolerance of the true plant (the ORACLE); the error trajectory

upstream_docs: Widrow & Hoff, Adaptive switching circuits, IRE WESCON 1960

human_capability_summary.built_to: fit a model to a system whose parameters are unknown or drifting, one sample at a time, from the error alone
human_capability_summary.pressure: unknown/drifting plant, noise, step-size stability limits
human_capability_summary.success_means: the weights converge to the plant's; tracking resumes after the plant changes

known_human_problem_solved: online system identification and adaptive filtering
human_environmental_pressure: unknown or time-varying plant, noise, real-time budget
human_failure_condition: step size too large: the weights diverge; too small: the filter cannot track the drift
behavioral_entry_point: change the plant's taps mid-run and watch re-convergence; raise mu past the stability bound

lineage_relations.note: the delta rule is LMS applied to a perceptron

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run padasip-1.2.2
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: fit a model to a system whose parameters are unknown or drifting, one sample at a time, from the error alone
